I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this is the safest way for me to use the whole year, spread my risk, and make sure I have a steady grain harvest. I will put all my land into winter wheat first, then follow with summer maize on the same fields after wheat harvest. I will not split too much land into other crops, because that adds more labor, more selling trouble, and more uncertainty. I want crops I know well, seed I can get easily, and management that fits local water and weather conditions.

For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, prepare the field with rotary tillage, and put on moderate fertilizer because wheat here responds well but too much input wastes money. I will irrigate a few key times, especially around overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling if water allows. I will spray only when needed for weeds, aphids, or disease. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield and better stand. I will keep tillage light and use no-tillage seeding after wheat if possible, because that saves time and helps keep moisture. I will fertilize mainly for strong early growth and grain filling, irrigate when the crop is stressed, and use a couple of pesticide sprays if pests or weeds become a problem. This is the plan I would follow for a steady and practical year.
